missingSafetyStop.evidence: Please stop using the machine now and unplug it.

rationale: The first reply asked about the smell type and gave a burning-smell stop-use warning, but it also listed a long set of cleaning steps, including drain filter work with the machine possibly still in use. After the customer described a burning smell, the second reply correctly told her to stop, unplug, avoid DIY inside the machine and contact the manufacturer. It listed likely causes as possibilities, not a single diagnosis. It also treated the haze as likely smoke and told her not to run even wash-only cycles, which is cautious but reasonable. It did not mention the overloading link in the second reply.
